answer: A busy wharf only lets ships dock after they post a bond that is slashed if they misbehave; an agent economy can do the same. Each agent stakes funds behind a persistent identity, and peers check its work before paying. A sybil operator on a knoll of fake accounts must fund every identity, so the cost of forging a crowd exceeds any gain. Reputation acts as a mirror: honest work compounds trust and higher-paying tasks, while one bad act reflects across all linked identities, making sock-puppet farms unprofitable.
